source.title_on_document: 생성형 AI 활용이 대학생의 창의적 아이디어 생성에 미치는 영향: 동일 과제 반복 수행에서의 사용 전환 효과 / The Effects of Generative AI Use on University Students' Creative Idea Generation: Switching Effects in Repeated Task Performance

supplement.where: The document mentions no supplementary material or online appendix.
supplement.holds: Nothing known. All reported statistics are in the main text (Tables 1-4, pp. 45-46, and prose on pp. 45-47).

paper_design_summary: 164 students at two Korean universities, in IT-related classes, did the task 'Imagining an Idea That Will Change the Future in 2035' twice in one session: Round 1 (10 min) with ChatGPT available (group A, n = 83) or without AI (group B, n = 81), then after a 30-minute break a Round 2 upgrade of their own ideas (10 min). Within each Round 1 group, participants were randomly split for Round 2 into keep AI (A1, 43) or stop AI (A2, 40), and adopt AI (B1, 41) or stay without AI (B2, 40). Two blind raters scored each participant's up to 10 ideas on a 4-dimension rubric summed to a 0-100 creativity total.

studies.label: Classroom experiment: Round 1 AI vs no AI, Round 2 randomized AI switching (idea generation, 2035 future ideas)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Round 2 switching condition, randomized within each Round 1 group: A (AI in Round 1) to keep AI (A1) or stop AI (A2); B (no AI in Round 1) to adopt AI (B1) or stay without AI (B2). How participants were placed in Round 1 groups A and B is not described; the document does not say Round 1 assignment was random.
assignment.quote: 2차에서는 1차 집단(A/B) 내부에서 무작위로 전환 조건을 분기하여 A는 AI 유지(A1) 또는 AI 중단(A2), B는 AI 도입(B1) 또는 미사용 유지(B2)로 배정한다.
assignment.locator: p. 44 (PDF p. 5), Section 3.1, step (3); also p. 41 (PDF p. 2), Introduction; Figure 1, p. 43 (PDF p. 4); mixed design (time within-subject, Round 2 condition between-subject) stated p. 43, Section 3.1

arms.name: A1 (AI maintained)
arms.description: Generative AI available in Round 1 and Round 2

arms.name: A2 (AI discontinued)
arms.description: Generative AI available in Round 1, removed in Round 2 upgrade

arms.name: B1 (AI adopted)
arms.description: No AI in Round 1, generative AI available in Round 2 upgrade

participants.exclusions: Only participants who wrote both the Round 1 and Round 2 outputs were included (p. 44). The number assigned and the number dropped are not stated.
participants.who: Students enrolled at two universities, taking IT-related courses; 121 male, 43 female; year and major not collected
participants.country: South Korea (stated as two domestic universities; authors at Soongsil University)
participants.quote: 분석에 포함된 참여자는 총 164명이며, 1차 조건은 A 83명, B 81명으로 구성되었다. 2차 조건은 A1 43명, A2 40명, B1 41명, B2 40명이다.
participants.locator: p. 44 (PDF p. 5), Section 3.1; repeated p. 45, Section 4.1; Figure 1, p. 43

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT (free plan) by default; other generative AI tools allowed if the participant wished
ai_tool.how_used: In AI conditions participants could use ChatGPT freely while writing ideas (Round 1) or while revising and elaborating their Round 1 ideas (Round 2 upgrade). Usage behavior was not measured (p. 44, p. 48).

task.description: 'Imagining an Idea That Will Change the Future in 2035': propose up to 10 ideas (software, products, services, policies) to improve life under future social changes. Round 2 asks participants to revise, supplement, and elaborate their Round 1 ideas or add new perspectives.
task.duration: Round 1 10 minutes; about 30-minute break (unrelated YouTube video); Round 2 10 minutes; one session

outcomes.name: Change in creativity total score from Round 1 to Round 2 (and Round 2 score): AI adoption, B1 vs B2
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two independent raters blind to condition scored each idea on novelty, usefulness/feasibility, elaboration/specificity, and future-change fit, summed to a 0-10 idea score; participant total = sum over up to 10 ideas (0-100); deductions of 1-3 points on novelty for duplicate or similar ideas within a round; mean of the two raters used. Rater expertise not stated. ICC (total, average of raters) .957 Round 1, .958 Round 2 (p. 45). Total mixes quantity and quality (mean ideas 9.18 Round 1, 9.52 Round 2; p. 44). Dimension-level results by arm are not reported.
outcomes.delay: Round 2 about 30 minutes after Round 1, same session

contrasts.locator: p. 46 (PDF p. 7), Table 4, Table 3, Section 4.4.2 item 1; Table 1 p. 45; model specification p. 45, Section 3.3.4

outcomes.name: Change in creativity total score from Round 1 to Round 2 (and Round 2 score): AI discontinuation, A1 vs A2
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same rubric total as S1-O1. In this contrast the treatment arm A1 kept AI in Round 2 and the control arm A2 produced its Round 2 output after AI was removed, so the control arm's output is unassisted post-AI work. The paper calls this the discontinuation effect (A1 gain - A2 gain).
outcomes.delay: Round 2 about 30 minutes after Round 1, same session

contrasts.locator: p. 47 (PDF p. 8), Section 4.4.2 item 2; p. 46 (PDF p. 7), Table 4, Table 3, Section 4.4.2; Table 1 p. 45

outcomes.name: Round 1 creativity total score: AI access (A) vs no AI (B)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same rubric total as S1-O1, on Round 1 output. The document does not say that Round 1 groups A and B were randomly assigned, so this contrast may not be randomized.

outcomes.name: Round 2 unassisted creativity total score after Round 1 AI use: A2 vs B2
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same rubric total as S1-O1. Both arms produced Round 2 without AI; A2 had AI in Round 1, B2 did not. The paper does not test this contrast; only arm descriptives in Table 4 are printed. Round 2 is an upgrade of each participant's own Round 1 draft, so A2's Round 2 output builds on AI-assisted Round 1 work. A vs B assignment is not stated as random.
outcomes.delay: Round 2 about 30 minutes after Round 1, same session

contrasts.treatment_arm: A2 (AI in Round 1, removed in Round 2)

eligibility.reason: Round 2 AI availability was randomly assigned within Round 1 groups (p. 44): B1 vs B2 (adopt AI vs no AI, 81 people analyzed) and A1 vs A2 (keep vs stop AI, 83 people analyzed), each above 50; 164 analyzed in the study. The outcome is a blind two-rater rubric creativity score of the ideas. Round 1 A vs B assignment is not described as random, so the H1 contrast (S1-O3) and the A2 vs B2 comparison (S1-O4) rest on non-randomized groups as far as the document states.

one_line_finding: Randomly giving AI in the Round 2 upgrade raised the creativity-score gain by 28.63 points (SE 2.49; B1 Δ 37.73 vs B2 Δ 9.10, 0-100 scale), and removing AI from prior users lowered it by 5.50 points (SE 2.47) relative to keeping it (pp. 46-47, Table 4).
open_questions: How Round 1 groups A and B were formed is not described; the 33-point Round 1 gap (d = 2.08) cannot be treated as a randomized estimate unless the authors confirm random assignment.
The A1 vs A2 contrast compares AI-available output with unassisted post-AI output; a reviewer may prefer to code it as after_ai rather than with_ai.
Rater background (lay or expert) is not stated; coded human_raters.
Number of students assigned before excluding those without both outputs is not stated.
notes: Other reported results not coded as outcomes: H2 within-person Round 1 vs Round 2 for the full sample (Round 1 46.57 SD 23.19, Round 2 60.93 SD 19.66; paired t(163) = 10.34, p < .001, mean gain 14.36, 95% CI [11.62, 17.10], dz = 0.81; p. 46, Table 2), a repetition effect with no AI contrast; H5 asymmetry (B1 - B2) - (A1 - A2) = 23.13, SE 3.51, z 6.60, p < .001, 95% CI [16.26, 30.00] (p. 47), a difference of the two coded contrasts. Mixed model: score ~ time x group_2 + (1 | individual), reference A1 (p. 45). Dimension-level ICCs over all 328 outputs are reported (p. 45) but dimension-level effects by arm are not. Average idea counts are reported for the whole sample only (9.18, 9.52), so no fluency outcome by arm. No diversity or similarity measure across people. Study run in actual class context with written consent; no IRB, preregistration, or data link stated. Design class coded field_rct because the paper calls it a classroom field experiment in IT courses (p. 44); lab_rct is an alternative reading.
